rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods - 2-year field trial (2019, 2020) at Faridkot and Abohar, RCBD with 8 treatments (SSDI x N levels, SF control, SDI control). Q2: Table 8 and 'Comparison of water use efficiency' - WUE under surface flood 57.0% versus 75.4-83.5% under SSDF and 80.9% under SDI; 'Effect of different treatments on water productivity indices' - irrigation water saving of 36-54% (Faridkot) and 52-61% (Abohar) under SSDI over SF in 2019, 20-50% in 2020. Q4: Tables 6-7 and 'Weather and site characteristics' - soil water balance components measured: surface runoff 86-93 mm and deep drainage 200-299 mm under SF versus far lower runoff and drainage under drip treatments, i.e. the loss pathways through which drip saves water were quantified.
rows.notes: Q3: WUE derived from one method (water meter plus soil-moisture-probe water balance) - no independent second method. Q5: only two sites, one crop, both sandy loam. Q6: plots of 60.75 m2. Q7: authors note 60% ETc gave poor efficiency and recommend adequate water at regular intervals, but WUE exceeded SF at all drip levels and no explicit requirement for the WUE advantage is stated; conservative 'no'. Q8: no limitations stated (drainage assumed zero under some conditions, upward flux ignored, but not framed as limitations). Q9: WUE reported without LSD or SD; LSD for BWP is a significance threshold, not a dispersion measure.

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods - own 2-year, two-location field experiment. Q2: Table 5, Abstract and Conclusion - SSDF at 80% ETc with 112.5 kg N/ha gave 3455 kg/ha SCY, 26.6% higher than surface flood (2728 kg/ha); SSDI 80% and 100% ETc gave 18.7% and 21% higher SCY than SF. Q4: 'Yield attributes and seed cotton yield' and Figure 4 - higher SCY attributed to measured boll count per plant (23-29% higher under SSDI 80/100% ETc than SF) and boll weight, and SCY shown to follow a linear relationship with measured actual crop ET (R2 0.72-0.98). Q7: 'Yield attributes' and 'Bio-physical water productivity' sections - SCY at 60% ETc (2619 kg/ha) fell below SF, authors state yield was optimized at 80% ETc and that irrigating with an adequate amount of water at regular intervals through drip, with 100% RDN, is needed to enhance SCY; Conclusion recommends 80% ETc with 112.5 kg N/ha.
rows.notes: Q3: single method (harvest weight of hand pickings). Q5: two locations only, one cultivar, same soil texture. Q6: plot scale. Q8: no limitations of the result stated. Q9: only LSD values given (Table 5), which function as significance thresholds like letter groupings; no SD, SE or CI for SCY.

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods - 2-year field trial at Faridkot and Abohar with SSDI, SDI and surface flood treatments. Q2: Tables 6-7 and 'Effect of different treatments on water productivity indices' - SSDI saved 36-54% (Faridkot) and 52-61% (Abohar) of irrigation water relative to SF in 2019 and 20-50% in 2020; Table 8 - WUE 75-84% under SSDF versus 57% under SF; Conclusion states SSDF saves irrigation water due to lesser drainage loss. Q4: Tables 6-7 - measured runoff (86-93 mm under SF vs 13-58 mm under SSDI) and deep drainage (200-299 mm under SF vs 69-139 mm under SSDI), the loss pathways through which SSDI conserves water.
rows.notes: Technology in passage is SSDI, which is the study's main treatment. Q3: one water-balance method. Q5: two sites, one crop. Q6: plot scale. Q7: no stated requirement for the water-saving effect from own findings. Q8: no limitations stated. Q9: no dispersion measure for water saving or WUE.

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods - own field experiment at two sites over two years.
rows.notes: The study does not measure weeds, weed control or any pest variable. It reports seed cotton yield, growth, water productivity, NUE, fiber quality and economics for SSDI vs SF and SDI. No own evidence on weed control, so Q2 is no. Technology (SSDI) matches, so not a technology mismatch; not an upstream precondition either.

notes: Full text available and complete. Study is a two-year, two-site plot experiment in Punjab, India on Bt cotton comparing SSDI at 60/80/100% ETc with two N fertigation levels against surface flood and surface drip controls. No explicit limitations section; statistics reported as LSD values only.
